MGIMS holds the National Workshop on Molecular Cytogenetic Techniques
Friday, 03 April 2026
1051 Hits
The National Level Hands-on Workshop on Molecular Cytogenetic Techniques in Clinical Practice was successfully organized by the Centre for Genetics & Genomics in collaboration with the  Departments of Anatomy and Paediatrics, of the Mahatma Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences, Sevagram, from the 9th to 13th March 2026. It  was a five-day intensive training program,attended by 15 participants from various medical colleges across the country. The workshop aimed to enhance participants’ hand on skills and understanding of advanced cytogenetic methods along with  their applications in clinical diagnostics.
The program featured expert lectures, live demonstrations, and practical training sessions on techniques such as fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH), karyotyping, and chromosomal analysis. Renowned experts like Dr Haldar from All India Institute of Medical Sciences, New Delhi, Dr Tarnekar from AIIMS, Nagpur, Dr Asoke Pal well known geneticist of national fame, Dr Anshu, MGIMS Sevagram, and Dr Priya Thakre from Wardha shared insights on recent advancements and clinical case studies, helping participants bridge the gap between theory and practice. The  key highlights were  the hands-on sessions conducted by Dr Prafulla Ambulkar and his team, where the  attendees gained practical laboratory experience on tissue culture to Karyotype preparation and FISH analysis under direct expert supervision. The workshop was much appreciated by all the participants who expressed their satisfaction and suggested that more such workshops should be conducted in future.
At the inauguration Dr Pratibha Narang, Chairperson of the workshop highlighted the importance of such workshops in the present scenario of molecular cytogenetic diagnostics where personalised medicine is fast evolving. At the valedictory function, Dr. B. S. Garg Secretary KHS,  emphasized the significance of genetic research in modern clinical practices, particularly in enhancing patient care outcomes. Dr A K  Shukla commended the participants for attending the intensive hands-on workshop on molecular cytogenetics and encouraged them to actively engage in genetic research and diagnostics at their respective institutions for improved patient services. Dr Prafulla Ambulkar, organising secretary expressed sincere gratitude to Kasturba Health Society President Shri P. L. Tapdiya Ji, and to the Anushandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF)  for their generous financial assistance in making this workshop a grand success. He also  thanked Dr Pratibha Narang, chairperson of the workshop,  Dr. Poonam Varma, MS Kasturba Hospital, Dr. Manish Jain, Dr. Jwalant Waghmare, Dr. Anshu, and Dr. Suchi Jain for their valuable support and guidance.
